Changes: General: Please note that MSOP Configurator v1.0.6 and MSOP Plugin v8.4.0 and all versions of these below are only compatible with MAME 0.200 to MAME 0.288 (unless MAME PR #15639 is applied to a custom MAME build). The upcoming official MAME 0.289+ release requires a new version of MSOP to work, as there is a fundamental change being implemented by the MAME devs that will prevent custom state outputs from being registered with MAME moving forward (and no code that enables this function will be allowed back into MAME). A new version of MSOP will be released in the near future that works around this limitation without the need for a custom MAME fork or build, and a working prototype is already undergoing testing.

Feature Added: Added support for Diagnostics page to automatically identify MSOP Plugin state outputs both with and without 'MSOP_' prefix on state outputs from MAME. This is an early feature preview that will be required for the upcoming changes to MSOP in the next major release.
UI Polish: Renamed the toggle for Sniffer/Hooker to Diagnostics in Diagnostics page. This should make more sense to most users regardless of the terms they're familiar with.
Architectural Overhaul: Renamed the latest zip files that are stored and downloaded from GitHub. Only MSOP Configurator v1.0.5+ will have access to MSOP Plugin v8.3.0+.

Feature Added: Added the ability to change the IP Address and Port in the Diagnostics page for the sniffer / hooker function. This means you can use MSOP Configurator to easily monitor other TCP Servers for debugging purposes (e.g. Sinden).

UI Polish: Changed Settings for MSOP Configurator to be radio buttons instead of a pill toggle. This should make things clearer to users since radio buttons are more appropriate for different options. Required rewrite of many functions to make this transition.

UI Polish: General tidy up of UI for consistency and neatness, such as resizing grids, adjusting corner radius, colours used for interactive elements, prevention of overflow when adjusting width, etc. There are many changes, and unfortunately too many to list out individually.

UI Polish: Enforced editable fields in the Diagnostics page (UI Refresh Rate, IP Address, and Port) to have validation checks performed. This prevents incorrect values entered by a user causing any potential issues.
UI Polish: Remade the Home page so that the layout is more condensed, informative, and optimised.
UI Polish: Renamed the toggle for Sniffer to Hooker in Diagnostics page since this is the term most users are familiar with.
UI Polish: Reordered the tabs and sub-tabs so that pages are easier to use and more predictable to locate.
UI Polish: Revised JSON syntax error notifications to make the issue clearer to the user so it can be easily identified and fixed.
Architectural Overhaul: Minor changes to the changelog.json structure for the MSOP Database Compiler.

Bug Fix: Resolved multiple Portable storage mode reliability issues by implementing accurate path resolution, adding smart directory wiping to protect nested configurations (like when storing MSOP_CONFIGURATOR.exe inside MAME > plugins > stateoutput), and introducing fail-safe rollbacks for interrupted storage migrations.

Bug Fix: Checkbox options in the MAME page were not being saved correctly in config.json after interactions. This affected the 'MAME Output Mode' and 'MAME Off-Screen Reload Compatibility' options, but these have now been fixed and work as expected.

Feature Added: Replaced old 'legacy' file detection for ini files and Lua scripts, and replaced it with more advanced logic that allows the user to keep detected ini files and Lua scripts if they opt out of the file removal, but if file removal is denied then no support can be provided for the MSOP Plugin as there is the potential for conflicts with those existing ini files and / or Lua scripts being kept.

Feature Added: Added new toggle in footer for 'Storage Mode'. If set to Standard (default), this will use your AppData > Roaming > MSOPsettings folder, which enables the MSOP Configurator to be opened from anywhere on your PC while keeping the exact same saved settings intact. If set to Portable, this will use the local MSOPsettings subfolder that is located within the same directory as your MSOP Configurator app, which is useful for backups of existing builds (useful if sharing a build that utilises MSOP).

Feature Added: Added new toggle in footer for 'Icon Type'. If set to Square (default), this will utilise the square variant of the MSOP icon and logo. If set to Round, this will utilise the round variant of the MSOP icon and logo.

ChangesPlugin: Note: As of 2026.07.03, MAME PR #15639 (https://github.com/mamedev/mame/pull/15639) has been rejected, and so MSOP Plugin v8.4.0 and below are only compatible with MAME 0.200 to 0.288 unless MAME PR #15639 is applied to a custom MAME 0.289+ build. A future MSOP update will be released shortly that will work without a custom MAME build, and is expected in MSOP Configurator v2.0.0+ and MSOP Plugin v9.0.0+ (both will be required moving forward, not just MSOP Plugin).

init.lua: Reworked logic so that MSOP Plugin complies with the requirements of MAME 0.289+ if PR #15639 is applied. Removed the logic that was added in MSOP Plugin v8.3.0 since that applied to PR #15618 instead. Fallback logic that existed previously is still in place for official releases of MAME 0.200 to 0.288.
readme.txt: Expanded 'Output Mappings' section so it is clear what state outputs need to be mapped to commands in MAMEhooker, OutputHooker, and/or QMamehook.

Note: As of 2026.07.01, MAME PR #15618 (https://github.com/mamedev/mame/pull/15618) has been rejected, and so a new pull request will be created with a different solution proposal to this problem. MSOP Plugin v8.3.0 at this time will be compatible with MAME 0.288 and below, or with MAME 0.289 and the PR 15618 applied to a custom MAME build.

init.lua: Implement 'Safe Setter' architecture. Centralises output management by abstracting Set_Output_Safe and Get_Output_Proxy, ensuring seamless compatibility between modern device-scoped MAME (0.289+) and legacy MAME releases.
init.lua: Implement 'Output Proxy Cache' function. Caches output_proxy objects at boot to eliminate redundant dictionary lookups and dynamic resolution overhead during the 60Hz frame loop.
init.lua: Encapsulate proxy resolution in pcall handlers. Prevents plugin crashes in environments lacking specific MAME API features, ensuring safe fallback to standard set_value operations.
readme.txt: Added 'Output Mappings' section so it is clear what state outputs need to be mapped to commands in MAMEhooker, OutputHooker, and/or QMamehook.

init.lua: Added new function RELOAD_MEM_MIN_VALUE so that if any number equal to or above this value is identified then this will trigger a reload (useful if games have multiple weapons that differ in ammo capacity, but you don't know the specific ammo available for each weapon).

init.lua: Expanded logic for GAME_STATUS_ACTIVE_VALUE so that an array can be used, which allows multiple values to be used (useful if the same memory address is shared between GAME_STATUS and ATTRACT_MODE_STATUS).
init.lua: Expanded logic for RELOAD_MEM_ADD_VALUE so that an array can be used, which allows multiple values to be used as triggers for reload (if they are known).
init.lua: Fixed logic used for ATTRACT_STATUS_ACTIVE_VALUE (this was incorrectly causing GAME_STATUS to override to 0 in some instances).
init.lua: Fixed code documentation so it reads more clearly to others.
init.lua: Removed accidental logic that in some cases would combine recoil and damage together.
readme.txt: Revised formatting and contents of readme file for MSOP Plugin.
init.lua: Added new feature to support enabling or disabling individual supported game ROMs with MSOP Plugin (in case MSOP causes clashes with custom scripts some users have for specific games).

init.lua: Added new feature that enables access to memory space as a 'region', which will hook directly into the physical ROM memory region instead of the CPU address space to allow safe patching (required in some instances for functions like Screen Flash removal).
init.lua: Added new feature that enables per player screen flash removal for games where each player can trigger a screen flash independently of each other.
init.lua: Added new feature that enables 64-bit data width for reading and writing memory address values.
init.lua: Fixed the PX_CreditsConsumed logic so that it correctly works for games where LIFE_DIRECTION = 'increase' (previously it was only working in games where LIFE_DIRECTION = 'decrease').

init.lua: Revised the PX_CreditsConsumed logic to account for instances where Player Status may change faster than the Credit counter can decrease. This will need to be checked against each game to check for logic edge cases.
init.lua: Fixed Damage and DamageTaken from triggering in certain edge cases when a player's life increases despite logic dictacting that an increase in life does not relate to a damage state event.

init.lua: Fixed flushing of warmup values when opening consecutive ROMs without fully exiting MAME between each ROM launch. This will ensure force feedback is disabled until a player is active in the game.
init.lua: Fixed ShotsFired and ShotsFiredPrimary so that in games where ammo may equal 0 but shots can still be fired at half rate, the counters will still continue to increase as appropriate.
init.lua: Minor tweaks to header text, plugin name, project information, and file purpose.

plugin.json: Changed plugin name to 'MAME State Output Project (MSOP)', changed 'date' to 'dateplugin', added 'datedatabase', and added 'channel'. These new values will require Configurator app v0.9.6+ to read properly.

readme.txt: Updated readme to elaborate on what the project is, how it works, and what command line options exist. I will elaborate on how init.lua and database.lua work with each other in more detail later.
readme.txt: Minor text changes as appropriate.
Bug Fix: Added safety clamp to check for recoil interval and hold interval being less than or equal to recoil duration.

Bug Fix: Fixed the counter for ShotsFiredPrimary so that it only counts shots fired based on 'Ammo' changes if Ammo is known, otherwise it will default to a simpler logic that will +1 for every recoil state event.
Bug Fix: If individual player credits are utilised for a game rather than global credits, then global credits will now equal the total combined number of individual player credits.

UX Improvement: Disabled debug OSD mode by default, which removes the text during ROM launch that states whether the active ROM is supported by the State Output Plugin (Not Supported = Dormant, Supported = Active).
Bug Fix: Fixed 'PX_Recoil' fallback logic if PX_Ammo is not known for the active ROM.
Bug Fix: Fixed 'PX_Recoil' logic for manual memory address polling (this was missed in the migration from the old Lua script architecture to the new plugin architecture).
Bug Fix: Fixed 'PX_Recoil' logic so that it doesn't freeze with a value of 1 (clashed with ammo math tracker, and would not reset back to 0 until another action reset the loop).
Bug Fix: Fixed logic for Demulshooter compatibility toggle (adds PX_Recoil and PX_Damaged state outputs with that specific naming convention).
Bug Fix: Fixed 'PX_Damage' not being triggered in logic when processing life lost state events.
Initial beta for testing state outputs using MAME plugin architecture.

v7 and below are incompatible with the Configurator app as they utilised the older MAME Lua Script architecture. This version is being included only for archival purposes, as it was the last Lua script based release for this project.

Note: As of 2026.07.03, MAME PR #15639 (https://github.com/mamedev/mame/pull/15639) has been rejected, and so MSOP Plugin v8.4.0 and below are only compatible with MAME 0.200 to 0.288 unless MAME PR #15639 is applied to a custom MAME 0.289+ build. A future MSOP update will be released shortly that will work without a custom MAME build, and is expected in MSOP Configurator v2.0.0+ and MSOP Plugin v9.0.0+ (both will be required moving forward, not just MSOP Plugin).

init.lua: Reworked logic so that MSOP Plugin complies with the requirements of MAME 0.289+ if PR #15639 is applied. Removed the logic that was added in MSOP Plugin v8.3.0 since that applied to PR #15618 instead. Fallback logic that existed previously is still in place for official releases of MAME 0.200 to 0.288.
readme.txt: Expanded 'Output Mappings' section so it is clear what state outputs need to be mapped to commands in MAMEhooker, OutputHooker, and/or QMamehook.

Note: As of 2026.07.01, MAME PR #15618 (https://github.com/mamedev/mame/pull/15618) has been rejected, and so a new pull request will be created with a different solution proposal to this problem. MSOP Plugin v8.3.0 at this time will be compatible with MAME 0.288 and below, or with MAME 0.289 and the PR 15618 applied to a custom MAME build.

init.lua: Implement 'Safe Setter' architecture. Centralises output management by abstracting Set_Output_Safe and Get_Output_Proxy, ensuring seamless compatibility between modern device-scoped MAME (0.289+) and legacy MAME releases.
init.lua: Implement 'Output Proxy Cache' function. Caches output_proxy objects at boot to eliminate redundant dictionary lookups and dynamic resolution overhead during the 60Hz frame loop.
init.lua: Encapsulate proxy resolution in pcall handlers. Prevents plugin crashes in environments lacking specific MAME API features, ensuring safe fallback to standard set_value operations.
readme.txt: Added 'Output Mappings' section so it is clear what state outputs need to be mapped to commands in MAMEhooker, OutputHooker, and/or QMamehook.

init.lua: Added new function RELOAD_MEM_MIN_VALUE so that if any number equal to or above this value is identified then this will trigger a reload (useful if games have multiple weapons that differ in ammo capacity, but you don't know the specific ammo available for each weapon).

init.lua: Expanded logic for GAME_STATUS_ACTIVE_VALUE so that an array can be used, which allows multiple values to be used (useful if the same memory address is shared between GAME_STATUS and ATTRACT_MODE_STATUS).
init.lua: Expanded logic for RELOAD_MEM_ADD_VALUE so that an array can be used, which allows multiple values to be used as triggers for reload (if they are known).
init.lua: Fixed logic used for ATTRACT_STATUS_ACTIVE_VALUE (this was incorrectly causing GAME_STATUS to override to 0 in some instances).
init.lua: Fixed code documentation so it reads more clearly to others.
init.lua: Removed accidental logic that in some cases would combine recoil and damage together.
readme.txt: Revised formatting and contents of readme file for MSOP Plugin.
init.lua: Added new feature to support enabling or disabling individual supported game ROMs with MSOP Plugin (in case MSOP causes clashes with custom scripts some users have for specific games).

init.lua: Added new feature that enables access to memory space as a 'region', which will hook directly into the physical ROM memory region instead of the CPU address space to allow safe patching (required in some instances for functions like Screen Flash removal).
init.lua: Added new feature that enables per player screen flash removal for games where each player can trigger a screen flash independently of each other.
init.lua: Added new feature that enables 64-bit data width for reading and writing memory address values.
init.lua: Fixed the PX_CreditsConsumed logic so that it correctly works for games where LIFE_DIRECTION = 'increase' (previously it was only working in games where LIFE_DIRECTION = 'decrease').

init.lua: Revised the PX_CreditsConsumed logic to account for instances where Player Status may change faster than the Credit counter can decrease. This will need to be checked against each game to check for logic edge cases.
init.lua: Fixed Damage and DamageTaken from triggering in certain edge cases when a player's life increases despite logic dictacting that an increase in life does not relate to a damage state event.

init.lua: Fixed flushing of warmup values when opening consecutive ROMs without fully exiting MAME between each ROM launch. This will ensure force feedback is disabled until a player is active in the game.
init.lua: Fixed ShotsFired and ShotsFiredPrimary so that in games where ammo may equal 0 but shots can still be fired at half rate, the counters will still continue to increase as appropriate.
